forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Procurements over £25,000 have generated £50,000 savings against estimated price to the end of Quarter 2, plus £70,000 cost avoidance.
news_drafts.lead: The savings are against the estimated price for procurements over £25,000, with cost avoidance from tendering or negotiating smaller procurements rather than using an incumbent or single quote.

news_drafts.headline: Council tax collection at 56.93% (£60 million of £105 million) at end of September 2026, which the paper states is on target.
news_drafts.lead: Business rates collection is 59.34% (£24 million of £40 million), also described as on target. Sundry debt outstanding is £0.95 million.

news_drafts.headline: Approval sought to reprofile £3.044 million of capital budgets into 2026/27 and future years, and remove £90,000 of schemes on completion.
news_drafts.lead: The reprofiling and removal reduce the external borrowing needed in 2026/27 and the MRP charge in 2027/28. The estimated underlying borrowing need for 2027/28 falls from the original budget by £1.611 million.

findings.headline: Procurements over £25,000 have generated £50,000 savings against estimated price to the end of Quarter 2, plus £70,000 cost avoidance.
findings.detail: The savings are against the estimated price for procurements over £25,000, with cost avoidance from tendering or negotiating smaller procurements rather than using an incumbent or single quote.
findings.matters: Procurement savings and cost avoidance are a measure a finance director elsewhere would compare, as they are rarely reported in cash terms against a budget line.
findings.figures: £50,000 savings; £70,000 cost avoidance; £95,000 combined cashable and cost avoidance savings
findings.quote: Procurements over £25,000 have generated £50,000 savings against the estimated price to the end of Quarter 2

findings.headline: Council tax collection at 56.93% (£60 million of £105 million) at end of September 2026, which the paper states is on target.
findings.detail: Business rates collection is 59.34% (£24 million of £40 million), also described as on target. Sundry debt outstanding is £0.95 million.
findings.matters: Collection rates are a direct check on the tax base a lender relies on, and a finance director elsewhere would compare them against their own profile.
findings.figures: 56.93% council tax collected; £60 million of £105 million; 59.34% business rates collected; £24 million of £40 million; £0.95 million sundry debt
findings.quote: is 56.93% (£60 million out of £105 million) which is on target

findings.headline: Approval sought to reprofile £3.044 million of capital budgets into 2026/27 and future years, and remove £90,000 of schemes on completion.
findings.detail: The reprofiling and removal reduce the external borrowing needed in 2026/27 and the MRP charge in 2027/28. The estimated underlying borrowing need for 2027/28 falls from the original budget by £1.611 million.
findings.matters: Reprofiling reduces near-term borrowing need and shifts MRP into later years, which a lender or finance director would weigh against future capital pressure.
findings.figures: £3.044 million reprofiled; £90,000 removed; £1.611 million lower borrowing need for 2027/28; £4.032 million revised 2027/28 borrowing forecast
findings.quote: Approval is sought to reprofile the £3.044 million as follows:.

findings.headline: Capital programme projected outturn of £13.169 million against a £16.304 million working budget, at 80% of budget.
findings.detail: The forecast underspend of £3.135 million reflects slippage on schemes into future years. The original capital budget was £12.48 million.
findings.matters: A capital programme delivering at 80% of its revised budget, with slippage into later years, is a pattern a finance director elsewhere would compare against their own delivery.
findings.figures: £13.169 million projected outturn; £16.304 million working budget; £3.135 million variance; £12.48 million original budget
findings.quote: The capital programme is showing a projected outturn of £13.169 million against a working budget of £16.304 million which is 80% of budget.

findings.headline: £171.46 million borrowed at end of September 2026: £90.46 million long term at 2.14%, and £81 million short term at 4.46%.
findings.detail: The paper splits external borrowing into long-term and short-term, with the short-term tranche carrying a higher average rate.
findings.matters: The gap between the short-term and long-term average rates, and the share of debt that is short-term, is the kind of refinancing exposure a lender or a peer finance director would examine.
findings.figures: £171.46 million total borrowed; £90.46 million long term at 2.14%; £81 million short term at 4.46%
findings.quote: the Council has £171.46 million borrowed, split as long term £90.46 million at an average rate of 2.14% and short term of £81 million at an average rate of 4.46%

daily_post.headline: Surrey Heath says it is below the reserve levels its chief financial officer has set, with a general fund balance of £538,000 against a £1.6 million target.
daily_post.lead: A council that is below its own reserve floor and expects to remain below it in every MTFS year has less buffer against shocks, which is a central question for lenders and peer finance directors.
